mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the historical development of the cell theory?
mcqs.explanation: Hooke first observed cell‑like structures in cork (1665). Leeuwenhoek later discovered living microorganisms (1674). Schwann (1839) and Schleiden (1838) formulated that the cell is the basic unit of animals and plants respectively. Finally, Virchow (1855) added that all cells arise from pre‑existing cells. This chronological order matches option A.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states the cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function.
options.C: Only plants are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of function; cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.D: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure; cells can arise spontaneously.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The classical cell theory has three postulates: (1) all living things are made of cells, (2) the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function, and (3) cells arise only from pre‑existing cells. Option A lists all three accurately; the other options introduce the disproved idea of spontaneous generation.

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes unicellular from multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life processes, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells forming tissues and organs.
options.B: Unicellular organisms have tissues, while multicellular organisms lack tissues.
options.C: Multicellular organisms consist of a single cell, whereas unicellular organisms have many cells.
options.D: Both unicellular and multicellular organisms have the same number of cells.

mcqs.answer: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all life processes, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells forming tissues and organs.
mcqs.explanation: Unicellular organisms (e.g., bacteria, amoeba) carry out all metabolic activities within one cell. Multicellular organisms (e.g., plants, animals) have many cells that differentiate into tissues and organs, allowing division of labor. Options B‑D are incorrect descriptions.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an exception to the classical cell theory?

options.A: Viruses are considered cells because they possess a nucleus and cytoplasm.
options.B: Viruses are non‑cellular entities that lack a true cellular organization, representing an exception to the cell theory.
options.C: Bacteria are not cells because they lack a membrane.
options.D: All living organisms, including viruses, are composed of cells.

mcqs.answer: Viruses are non‑cellular entities that lack a true cellular organization, representing an exception to the cell theory.
mcqs.explanation: Viruses do not have a cellular structure, cannot carry out metabolism on their own, and thus do not satisfy the three postulates of cell theory, making them an exception. Options A, C, and D incorrectly treat viruses or bacteria as cells.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which historical observation directly supported the first postulate of the cell theory that all living organisms are composed of cells?

options.A: Hooke’s observation of cork tissue revealing a ‘cellular’ structure.
options.B: Mendel’s experiments on pea plant inheritance.
options.C: Darwin’s observations on finch beak variations.
options.D: Ohm’s formulation of the law of electrical resistance.

mcqs.answer: Hooke’s observation of cork tissue revealing a ‘cellular’ structure.
mcqs.explanation: Robert Hooke, using a microscope in 1665, observed hollow compartments in cork and coined the term ‘cell’, providing the first concrete evidence that living matter is made up of discrete units. The other options relate to genetics, evolution, or physics, not cell theory.

mcqs.question: A student writes three statements about cells. Which set of statements correctly represents the cell theory?

options.A: 1) All living organisms are composed of cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of structure and function. 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: 1) All living organisms are composed of cells. 2) Cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter. 3) The cell is the basic unit of structure and function.
options.C: 1) Only plants are composed of cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of function. 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.D: 1) All living organisms are composed of cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of structure. 3) Cells can arise spontaneously.

mcqs.answer: 1) All living organisms are composed of cells. 2) The cell is the basic unit of structure and function. 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the three universally accepted postulates of the cell theory. Options B and D incorrectly include spontaneous generation, and option C incorrectly limits cells to plants.

mcqs.question: Identify the misconception in the following statement: "All bacteria are multicellular organisms."

options.C: Partially true – some bacteria are multicellular.
options.D: Cannot be determined without more information.

mcqs.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotic microorganisms that exist as single cells; they do not form tissues or organs. Hence the statement is false. Options A, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Why are viruses considered exceptions to the cell theory?

options.A: Because they lack cellular structure and cannot carry out metabolism independently.
options.B: Because they possess a true nucleus and mitochondria.
options.C: Because they reproduce by binary fission like bacteria.
options.D: Because they are composed of multiple cells.

mcqs.answer: Because they lack cellular structure and cannot carry out metabolism independently.
mcqs.explanation: Viruses do not have a membrane-bound cell structure, lack organelles, and depend on host cells for metabolism and replication, violating all three postulates of the cell theory. Options B, C, and D describe features that viruses do not have.
